p1: In 1872, a ship was found drifting across the Atlantic... with nobody on board.
Her name was the Mary Celeste.
On November 7th, she left New York for Genoa, Italy. Ten people aboard.
A month later, the crew of the Dei Gratia spotted her near the Azores.
They climbed aboard. Nobody was there.
The ship was seaworthy. There was still food and water.
The crew's belongings were still in their quarters.
More than 1,700 barrels of alcohol... still in the hold.
But the only lifeboat was gone.
So were the captain's navigation instruments.
One of the pumps had been taken apart. There were over three feet of water in the hold.
The last log entry: November 25th. After that... nothing.
A court in Gibraltar found no sign of foul play.
So why would ten people leave a safe ship... for one small boat?
None of them were ever seen again.
